results.content: We introduce LocoMamba, a vision-driven cross-modal DRL framework built on selective state-space models, specifically leveraging Mamba, that achieves near-linear-time sequence modeling, effectively captures long-range dependencies, and enables efficient training with longer sequences. Despite this, current cross-modal fusion architectures face critical limitations: recurrent models suffer from vanishing gradients and poor long-horizon modeling, hierarchical designs complicate optimization, and Transformer-based models incur quadratic computational and memory costs with sequence length, constraining resolution and training efficiency. To address these challenges, this work introduces LocoMamba, a vision-driven end-to-end DRL framework that leverages the selective state-space model Mamba as a fusion backbone. LocoMamba encodes proprioceptive states and depth images into compact tokens, which are fused via stacked Mamba layers using selective state-space scanning with near-linear time complexity. LocoMamba’s architecture is structured into three end-to-end trainable components: input encoding, cross-modal fusion via Mamba, and policy optimization. The fusion backbone consists of stacked Mamba selective state-space model (SSM) layers, which process the token sequence through input-dependent, recurrent state updates.
